forest.statement:
Optimize the supplied baseline on one NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3. Use the real independent AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy. Choose useful topics yourself.
Compute exactly the supplied eighth-order Y derivative on a fixed 64x64x64 FP32 mesh. Preserve the supplied periodic halo convention (period 63 at the endpoints) and coefficients 63*[4/5,-1/5,4/105,-1/280]. Inputs vary and may be signed. Compare to an independent double-precision scalar oracle with abs error <=5e-5+2e-6*abs(reference).
Edit only src/candidate.cu. Preserve the extern C host entry point:
void run(const float*A,const float*B,float*C,float*scratch,int n,int m,int k,float alpha,float beta).
The host provides contiguous device buffers, n=m=k for square matrices, and scratch of at least n*n+65536 floats (64^3+65536 for the derivative). A and B are read-only. C must be fully produced. Do not overwrite any buffer or allocate beyond the declared storage. Scratch contents must not be assumed initialized between calls. The call uses the default CUDA stream; custom device helper functions and multiple launches are allowed. The full run is timed using CUDA events, with allocation, transfers, compilation and correctness checks excluded. Use actual CUDA source, no external optimized math library calls or other resources. Do not read files, environment variables, timers or benchmark state to detect inputs or phases. No persistent cached answers; every invocation must compute its output for the current input. Input dimensions and valid numerical invariants may be specialized.
The driver and oracle are protected. Development harness checks only search inputs; fresh confirmation uses independent seeds. Candidate GPU tests are serialized by the controller. Record failures and measured evidence, integrate after research closes, and independently confirm final G. No new allocations. The published optimized implementations are withheld from the source workspace.

decision.rationale: Demander un essai d’intégration mesuré, sans présumer d’un gain : partir du meilleur programme correct, T2 32×16 (2,901 μs), et adapter le blocage de deux sorties y par thread de T3 (94ee21b6e9dd4f08, 2,976 μs). Hypothèse concrète : produire 32 lignes y par bloc avec 16 fils y, chacun calculant deux sorties, conserver un halo partagé de rayon 4 et viser 512 fils plutôt que le bloc 32×32 de 1024 fils essayé par 4bf3de724d1e4f6f (3,094 μs). Cela peut réduire le nombre de blocs et le surcoût des halos sans les blocs de 1024 fils, mais le surplus de ressources partagées et de travail par fil peut annuler le gain. Garder exactement les coefficients, l’arithmétique, la couverture de sortie et le repliement y période 63; vérifier l’oracle et mesurer la latence complète.

Terminer après l’intégration mesurée : le candidat combiné f42f92e86c6e4a1a est correct à 2,941 μs, mais plus lent que sa base correcte 264197d63c124b41 à 2,901 μs. Les résultats disponibles ne justifient pas une nouvelle combinaison; laisser le contrôleur retenir le meilleur programme vérifié et confirmer G indépendamment.

children.objective: Implement and measure a single-pass direct-global stencil with one output per thread and no shared memory or block-wide barriers. Map warp lanes to contiguous x elements; compare practical launch mappings and unroll the eight neighbor terms. Reproduce the baseline y-halo mapping for every offset, produce all 64³ outputs from current A on every call, and use no extra launch or allocation. Validate against the independent oracle and compare full-run event latency with the baseline.
children.subject: Coalesced direct-global stencil without shared memory

children.objective: Explore shared-memory pencil geometry as a contrast to the supplied 4-by-64 block. Compare wider x pencils while retaining the full 64-row y slab (for example, 8- or 16-wide x pencils) against x-wide blocks producing smaller y subtiles with radius-4 halos. Measure the tradeoff between improved x coalescing, block count, halo duplication, synchronization, and occupancy; do not assume either shape wins. Preserve the exact stencil coefficients and baseline y-halo/period-63 endpoint mapping, cover every output, validate against the independent oracle for varying signed inputs, and compare full-run event latency. Use only the existing buffers and allowed launch model.
children.subject: Shared-memory pencil geometry: full-height versus y-subtile tiling

children.objective: Implement and measure register-blocked y outputs: assign contiguous x elements across warp lanes and have each thread compute multiple nearby y outputs, reusing their overlapping input neighborhood in registers rather than shared memory. Explore a small number of outputs per thread and suitable launch geometry; preserve exact coefficients and baseline halo mapping, compute every output from current A, and use no additional allocation or launch. Compare oracle correctness and full-run latency.
children.subject: Register reuse across multiple y outputs

plan.analysis: Choose N=3 because the baseline suggests three distinct single-kernel strategies worth testing, not to meet a preset tree count. The measured baseline is correct, with three samples averaging 3.494 μs; no profiling or child measurements are available, so coalescing and synchronization are hypotheses to test rather than proven bottlenecks. In the supplied kernel, a block spans 4 x positions and 64 y positions, uses shared memory, and executes two block barriers. The proposed trees separately test eliminating shared memory, improving x-wide shared tiling, and reusing loads across multiple y outputs in registers. The CUDA 12.6.3 Best Practices Guide discusses coalescing and strided access (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.6.3/cuda-c-best-practices-guide/index.html, §9.2.1); this supports the rationale, not a performance prediction. Preserve the supplied 64³ FP32 operation, coefficients, exact y-halo convention (including the period-63 endpoint handling), tolerance, full C output, entry point, and buffer/allocation constraints. The supplied target is NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3; no exact compiler version or device-counter evidence is available.
